nodes.title: Almost coherent sheaves on formal models
nodes.statement: For a qcqs admissible formal O_C-scheme 𝔛, with I=(p) and almost ideal 𝔪_C, an almost sheaf Fᵃ is almost adically quasi-coherent when its left-adjoint representative F! is I-adically complete with quasi-coherent reductions on every formal affine. It is almost coherent when locally its module of sections is almost finitely presented. D_acoh(𝔛)ᵃ is the full subcategory of D(O_𝔛ᵃ) whose cohomology sheaves have this property. The same notation on 𝔛₀ denotes almost quasi-coherent almost coherent sheaves on the scheme modulo p.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply the abstract Serre quotient of modules and sheaves supplied by P0 to (O_C,𝔪_C).
Use completed localization on each formal affine and glue; use AC Lemma 4.5.22 to identify almost finite presentation with almost coherence in this adhesive setup.
Define the derived subcategory by cohomology, using the almost coherent weak Serre property; do not define it using all adically quasi-coherent sheaves as an abelian category.
acceptance: The formal and scheme-modulo-p categories agree on sheaves killed by p.

nodes.title: Almost nearby-cycle complexes
nodes.statement: For an admissible formal O_C-scheme 𝔛 with d-dimensional generic fibre X, write ν:X_proét→𝔛_Zar for the specialization morphism of ringed sites and μ:X_proét→X_an for the analytic one. Compute locally on toric perfectoid covers with almost purity and continuous cochains; sheafify the resulting finite-range almost coherent cohomology.

nodes.title: Formal dualizing complexes and canonical sheaves
nodes.statement: For a separated flat admissible formal O_K-scheme 𝔛 with pure relative dimension d, put 𝔛_n=𝔛×Spec(O_K/pⁿ), n≥1. Choose compatible scheme dualizing complexes ω•_{𝔛_n}=f_n!O_K/pⁿ and define ω•_𝔛=Rlim_n ω•_{𝔛_n}. Its isomorphism class is independent of choices, but no canonical identification of these complexes is asserted. The bottom sheaf ω_𝔛=H⁻ᵈ(ω•_𝔛) is canonical and O_K-flat. The complex is coherent of amplitude [−d,0], reduces derivedly to ω•_{𝔛_n}, and for smooth 𝔛 is Ω̂ᵈ_{𝔛/O_K}[d].
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply coherent f! over O_K/pⁿ, using its flat-finite-presentation amplitude theorem, and choose compatible reductions.
Take the derived inverse limit; use coherence and derived completeness to identify derived reductions.
Extract the bottom sheaf from the compatible system; use torsion-freeness over the valuation ring for its flatness. Universally coherent f! is G1.
acceptance: The modulo-p dualizing complex is a derived reduction of ω•_𝔛, not generally the sheaf ω_𝔛/p in degree −d alone.

For a separated qcqs admissible O_K-model 𝔛 with smooth pure-d generic fibre X and geometrically reduced residue special fibre, there is a canonical s_𝔛:Ωᵈ_{X/K}≅(ω_𝔛)_K and an identification Ωᵈ_X[d]≅(ω•_𝔛)_K. The bottom identification is independent of algebraization and compatible with proper rig-isomorphisms between models with these hypotheses. The complex comparison is not asserted to be canonical.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
The construction in Z §2.7 uses an algebraically closed base field; only the preceding formal duality targets are asserted over general K.
proofSteps: Use refined local algebraization G2 for models with geometrically reduced residue special fibre.
Apply smooth algebraic duality after inverting p and compare completions.
Check independence using algebraization comparisons and the bottom trace for proper rig-isomorphisms. Reduced-model cofinality G2 supplies models in this class when constructing the rigid trace.
acceptance: On the formal torus, s sends the wedge of dlog coordinates to the generic canonical generator.

nodes.title: Coherent traces on smooth rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Over the algebraically closed field C, for a proper morphism f:Y→X of smooth separated qcqs rigid C-spaces, both pure of dimension d, define Tr_f:f_*Ωᵈ_Y→Ωᵈ_X by a proper map of admissible models and their bottom trace, transported by s. The map is independent of models, composes, and for finite étale f equals the coefficient trace under Ωᵈ_Y≅f^*Ωᵈ_X. Pullback in this last formula is the usual inverse image of differential bundles.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
The model-independent construction uses the algebraically closed setting of Z §2.7 and its reduced-model cofinality input G2.
proofSteps: Choose a formal representative after admissible blow-ups and take the generic fibre of its bottom trace.
Use cofinal common models and the trace comparison for rig-isomorphisms to show independence.
Algebraize finite étale maps on a dense smooth open and compare the multiplication trace; extend using coherent generic-fibre descent.
acceptance: For a finite étale map of degree r, Tr_f(f^*α)=rα, including r divisible by p.

nodes.title: Torsion-free nearby cohomology
nodes.statement: For n≥0 and any admissible formal O_C-model, define R̃ⁿν_*Ô⁺ as Rⁿν_*Ô⁺ modulo its p-power torsion, equivalently modulo its (ζ_p−1)-power torsion. It is an honest O_𝔛-module with no O_C-scalar torsion. Cup products descend, and cup of n degree-one classes factors through the exterior power, also for p=2.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Quotient by the union of kernels of scalar powers; p and ζ_p−1 generate cofinal power ideals.
Descend cup products using their scalar linearity.
Graded commutativity gives 2x²=0; for p=2 the quotient is 2-torsion-free, so x²=0.
acceptance: The infinite-power torsion quotient cannot be replaced by the kernel of one scalar without a separate theorem.

nodes.title: BMS maps on admissible models
nodes.statement: For every admissible formal O_C-model and n≥1, construct Φⁿ:Ω̂ⁿ_{𝔛/O_C}{−n}→R̃ⁿν_*Ô⁺. In degree one use the p-completed absolute cotangent map and H⁰(L̂_{O_𝔛/Z_p})=Ω̂¹, H⁰(Rν_*L̂_{Ô⁺/Z_p})=R¹ν_*Ô⁺{1}; then quotient torsion. Higher Φⁿ are exterior cup powers. These maps are functorial under flat morphisms and commute with étale restriction.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use cotangent transitivity O_C/Z_p and the perfectoid vanishing on the pro-étale basis.
Take degree zero, untwist and pass to the torsion quotient.
Take exterior powers and cup; obtain flat functoriality from the cotangent transformation and flat base change.
acceptance: The input twist is the Breuil–Kisin twist {−n}, not the Tate twist (−n).

nodes.title: Smooth integral Hodge–Tate inverse
nodes.statement: For a smooth pure-d formal model, Rⁿν_*Ô⁺/Rⁿν_*Ô⁺[ζ_p−1]=R̃ⁿ is finite locally free, and Φⁿ identifies Ω̂ⁿ{−n} with (ζ_p−1)ⁿR̃ⁿ. Divide onto this image and use the dual Fontaine dlog map to obtain the canonical Ψ′ⁿ:R̃ⁿ→Ω̂ⁿ(−n). In degree d, compose the quotient and Ω̂ᵈ≅ω to get Ψᵈ:Rᵈν_*Ô⁺→ω(−d). Here n≥1; set Φ⁰=Ψ′⁰=id on the unit sheaf, which defines the dimension-zero trace.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply BMS Hodge–Tate comparison after Lη_{ζ_p−1}; use its cohomology formula to identify the single-scalar and power-torsion quotients.
Check the image of Φ¹ using the cotangent truncation and obtain all degrees by the multiplicative comparison.
Combine Φ inverse on its scalar image with dlog-dual on twists. Independence of a root-of-unity trivialization follows from the intrinsic dlog map.
acceptance: Do not select an isomorphism O_C{1}≅O_C(1) without its dlog scaling factor.

nodes.title: Rational Hodge–Tate normalization and traces
nodes.statement: For a nice model, the generic fibre of Φⁿ is Scholze’s canonical Ωⁿ_X(−n)≅Rⁿμ_*Ô_X, after applying the Fontaine dlog change of twists. In torus coordinates dlog T_i corresponds to the i-th coordinate character of Γ=Z_p(1)ᵈ. Consequently the generic Ψ is its inverse, and it commutes with finite étale traces on top differentials and pro-étale cohomology.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the existing rational Hodge–Tate comparison of P8; verify its coordinate normalization on G_m and products by the Kummer character.
Compare the BMS cotangent cocycle with Fontaine dlog in the one-coordinate case, then exterior powers.
Reduce to a dense smooth open with finite étale toric coordinates and extend equality of vector-bundle maps on the connected smooth generic fibre.

Correct Z equation (3.7) as recorded in E21: after inversion use Ψ′=j∘Φ⁻¹=Sch⁻¹, with no additional scalar on the source. This agrees with the smooth integral inverse, whose defining square uses inclusion of the image lattice.
For finite étale f, compare multiplication trace with the pro-étale counit, using the algebra trace calculation.
acceptance: Coordinate tori suffice for normalization; no splitting of the entire Hodge–Tate complex is asserted.
On the one-dimensional torus, Ψ′ sends the normalized coordinate character back to dlog T with its Tate twist; a residual factor (1−ζ_p)⁻¹ would fail this normalization.

nodes.title: Nice formal models
nodes.statement: A nice model of dimension d is a qcqs separated admissible formal O_C-scheme whose generic fibre is smooth of pure dimension d and whose residue special fibre modulo 𝔪_C is reduced. Its reduction modulo p need not be reduced. A separated qcqs smooth model of pure dimension d is nice; the local theory is extended to non-quasi-compact spaces by restriction to the qcqs opens to which the statements apply.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Conjoin the three geometric conditions with the ambient qcqs convention for this packet.
Use perfection of the residue field to pass between reduced and geometrically reduced residue fibres in this O_C setting.
acceptance: Niceness is stable under étale restriction; it is not a chosen smooth formal model.

nodes.title: Integral and mod-p Faltings traces
nodes.statement: For a nice d-model, there is a unique honest integral map Tr_F^{d,+}:Rᵈν_*Ô⁺→ω_𝔛(−d) agreeing with Ψᵈ on the formal smooth locus and with the generic inverse Hodge–Tate map. Truncate the almost integral complex to obtain A_𝔛→ω_𝔛ᵃ(−d)[−d]. Derived reduction modulo p and the canonical bottom inclusion give Tr_F:K_𝔛→ω•_{𝔛₀}ᵃ(−d)[−2d].
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the Hartogs kernel to glue the two maps into the canonical sheaf.
Use almost amplitude ≤d to project A_𝔛 to Hᵈ(A_𝔛)[−d], then apply the honest map after almostification.
Reduce derivedly and compose ω_𝔛/p[−d]→ω•_{𝔛₀}[−2d], obtained from the bottom-cohomology map; this gives the mod-p trace.
acceptance: For a smooth model ω•_{𝔛₀}=Ωᵈ[d], so the target becomes Ωᵈᵃ(−d)[−d]. The [−2d] is essential in the singular presentation.

nodes.title: Finite pro-étale traces and model pushforwards
nodes.statement: For finite étale f:Y→X, the exact pro-étale pushforward has its counit Tr:f_*Ô_Y⁺→Ô_X⁺, defined by summation on a splitting cover. It extends to Ô and O⁺/pⁿ, and to R f₀_*K_𝔜→K_𝔛 for formal representatives. Its generic fibre agrees with the rational trace. Push forward through the specialization diagram to define model traces.
Check locally on a split perfectoid cover; identify summation with the algebra trace and descend.

nodes.title: Polystable formal models
nodes.statement: For blocks i=1,…,l with n_i≥0 and 0≠ϖ_i∈O_C, a standard polystable algebra is R⁺=O_C⟨t_{i,j}:0≤j≤n_i⟩/(∏_j t_{i,j}−ϖ_i for every i). Its relative dimension is d=Σ_i n_i. A polystable formal scheme admits an étale cover with étale maps to such models. Unit ϖ_i are allowed; zero ϖ_i are excluded. A separated qcqs polystable model of pure dimension d is nice; on such a model ω is invertible with ω•≅ω[d].
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the monomial relations to prove O_C-flatness and topological finite presentation.
The nonzero parameters give smooth generic fibres; reduction gives a product of normal-crossing monomial hypersurfaces.
Apply complete-intersection duality on algebraic charts and formal étale comparison to get the invertible bottom sheaf.
acceptance: A polystable chart is a product of blocks, not just a single semistable equation.

nodes.title: Polystable root towers
nodes.statement: Choose compatible p-power roots of each nonzero ϖ_i. Let R_m⁺ be the same block algebra in t_{i,j}^{1/p^m} with block product ϖ_i^{1/p^m}, and R_∞⁺ the p-completed direct limit. The generic inverse limit is affinoid perfectoid and a pro-étale Γ-torsor over Spa(R⁺[1/p],R⁺), where Γ consists of the root-of-unity actions with product one in each block, hence Γ≅Z_p(1)ᵈ. Each finite stage is finite and finitely presented over R⁺ and O_C-flat; it need not be R⁺-flat.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Adjoin roots subject to the block-product conditions and form the completed colimit.
Verify Frobenius surjectivity modulo p and the integral perfectoid criterion on monomials.
Invert p to identify finite étale root covers and their inverse-limit torsor; use the product-one constraints to compute Γ.
acceptance: Keep O_C-flatness distinct from R⁺-flatness at finite level.

nodes.title: Character summands of polystable towers
nodes.statement: Let T be the block-product-one torus and L=X*(T)=⊕_i(Z^{n_i+1}/Z·(1,…,1)). Every χ∈L[1/p] has a unique representative with nonnegative rational exponents and minimum zero in each block. Let V_χ be the O_C-line generated by that monomial. Then R_m⁺ is the p-completed sum of V_χ for χ∈p⁻ᵐL. For χ̄∈L[1/p]/L define R⁺_{χ̄} as the completed sum over χ+L. This yields a finite direct sum at level m and a completed direct sum at infinity. Multiplication V_χV_ψ⊂V_{χ+ψ} has a parameter factor and is not generally an isomorphism.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Normalize exponents by subtracting the minimum separately in each block.
Prove uniqueness of the resulting monomial expansion in the completed algebra.
Regroup by integral-character cosets; the Γ action is scalar on each coset. Retain the scalar factor created when a product requires a new normalization.
acceptance: The two false strong-grading assertions in Z are corrected by E13; no later argument uses them.

nodes.title: Character cohomology and nearby-cycle comparison
nodes.statement: For a standard polystable chart, sheafified continuous cochains C_cont(Γ,R_∞⁺)→Rν_*Ô⁺ are an almost isomorphism. Choose a basis of Γ. Koszul cochains compute the completed character summands: the trivial character has exterior cohomology of ranks binomial(d,i); every nontrivial finite-level character cohomology is annihilated by ζ_p−1, and is almost finitely presented with no 𝔪_C-torsion. The annihilator estimates improve with growing p-power denominators, giving the small tails used in completed sums.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply almost purity and Cartan–Leray on the generic perfectoid Γ-torsor, then sheafify over formal affines.
For a character of order pᵐ, one Koszul scalar generates the ideal (ζ_{pᵐ}−1); compute its exterior residual complex and annihilator.
Use uniform torsion bounds and completed-sum cohomology. Distinguish annihilation by ζ_p−1 from almost-zero annihilation by all of 𝔪_C.
acceptance: For a nontrivial character, H⁰ vanishes because the summand is O_C-torsion-free; positive cohomology may be nonzero torsion.

nodes.title: Integral décalage and the polystable top map
nodes.statement: For a polystable chart, applying Lη_{1−ζ_p} to the almost continuous-cochain comparison gives an honest isomorphism. Rⁱν_*Ô⁺ modulo its (1−ζ_p)-torsion is locally free of rank binomial(d,i). The top integral Faltings map induces an isomorphism Rᵈν_*Ô⁺/[1−ζ_p]≅ω_𝔛(−d), where brackets mean the torsion submodule, not the principal-ideal quotient.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Prove the special décalage criterion using the cone’s almost-zero cohomology and absence of 𝔪_C-torsion in the relevant derived reductions. An arbitrary almost isomorphism does not become an isomorphism under Lη.
Use the character computations to verify that criterion, then compute Lη cohomology by the imported formula.
On the top trivial-character line identify the trace on the generic fibre and use the torsion-free line to conclude.
acceptance: The quotient removes scalar torsion; reducing a locally free module modulo 1−ζ_p would give a different, torsion module.

nodes.title: Root-stage projection traces
nodes.statement: For a standard polystable chart, define tr_m⁺:R_m⁺→R⁺ by projection onto the integral-character coset summand in the finite decomposition. In characteristic p the analogous map tr_m:A_m→A for A=F_p[t₀,…,t_n]/(t₀⋯t_n) is the monomial projection onto the base-ring summand in the pᵐ-root algebra A_m. These are module maps normalized by tr_m(1)=1; they are not the ordinary algebra trace of a degree-divisible-by-p extension.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Define the characteristic-p monomial projection, retaining exactly the weights integral in L.
Use the direct-sum coset projection for the integral tower.
Verify compatibility with products by elements of the base ring and with finite-level inclusions.
acceptance: For m=0 the map is identity.

nodes.title: Derived duality of finite root algebras
nodes.statement: For the characteristic-p monomial hypersurface A and every m≥0, multiplication followed by tr_m induces A_m≅RHom_A(A_m,A). For every standard polystable R⁺, the integral projection similarly gives R_m⁺≅RHom_{R⁺}(R_m⁺,R⁺); characterwise R⁺_χ≅RHom_{R⁺}(R⁺_{−χ},R⁺). These modules need not be projective or flat over the singular base.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: In characteristic p, use the hypersurface resolution/duality and the explicit monomial projection to identify Hom and prove higher Ext vanishing; retain the singular relation in this computation.
For a single nonunit-parameter block choose π with |π|>|ϖ^{1/pᵐ}| and |π|>|p|; reduce to the characteristic-p hypersurface after derived reduction.
Use derived completeness, Hom base change and derived Nakayama to lift the isomorphism; for unit parameters use the free torus decomposition.
Combine blocks by the completed derived Künneth comparison, whose finite-presentation and O_C-flatness hypotheses hold for the root stages; extract opposite-character pairs.
acceptance: For a nodal chart, duality must be formulated by derived Hom; a declaration requiring all R⁺_χ to be free over R⁺ would reject the required example.

nodes.title: Oriented continuous-cochain traces
nodes.statement: A basis of Γ≅Z_pᵈ identifies the top cohomology of its Koszul complex with its coefficient module. For trivial Γ action on R⁺, projection to Hᵈ defines tr_Γ:C_cont(Γ,R⁺)→R⁺[−d]. Compose C_cont(Γ,R_∞⁺)→C_cont(Γ,R⁺), induced by projection to the integral-character summand, with tr_Γ. A basis change multiplies this scalar trace by its determinant; restoring the Tate orientation line makes the geometric pairing intrinsic.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the Koszul top wedge for the ordered basis and the trivial action.
Project coefficients to the trivial coset and compose the trace in the derived category.
Track the top exterior line under basis change rather than declaring the scalar trace canonical.
acceptance: For d=0 the trace is the identity on the trivial coefficient ring.

nodes.title: Almost duality of polystable continuous cochains
nodes.statement: Let B=C_cont(Γ,R_∞⁺). The oriented cup trace pairing B⊗ᴸ_{R⁺}B→R⁺[−d] is perfect after almostification: Bᵃ≅RalHom_{R⁺ᵃ}(Bᵃ,R⁺ᵃ)[−d]. Before passing to all characters, the Koszul pairing for each opposite pair R⁺_χ,R⁺_{−χ} is a derived duality. The comparison of the completed character sum with its dual product is an almost isomorphism.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use Koszul self-duality and opposite-character root-module duality for each finite character.
Show the internal Homs are derived p-complete before passing to the completed sum.
Estimate the cokernel of the sum-to-product map using the improving high-denominator annihilators; it is killed by every small ideal, hence almost zero.
acceptance: Ordinary direct sums cannot simply be interchanged with dual products; the almost tail estimate is part of the proof.

nodes.title: Good formal quotients
nodes.statement: A good quotient is a finite quotient morphism f:𝔛′→𝔛=𝔛′/G between nice d-models, for a finite group G acting over O_C, with 𝔛′ having quasiprojective residue special fibre and f_C a finite étale G-torsor. The group order may be divisible by p. Quasiprojectivity of that fibre and the formal quotient theorem are the geometric existence hypotheses, supplied through G2; this node names the proof-specific class of quotient diagrams.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use a finite formal quotient of the specified quasiprojective model, then require niceness and the generic torsor condition.

nodes.title: Almost local duality descends along good quotients
nodes.statement: For a good quotient f:𝔛′→𝔛 put B=R f₀_*K_𝔛′ with its derived G-action. Restriction gives K_𝔛≅B^{hG}, while trace gives B_{hG}≅K_𝔛. If β_𝔛′ is perfect, then β_𝔛 is perfect. These two isomorphisms come from torsor Shapiro descent, not a norm isomorphism for arbitrary G-modules.

proofSteps: On a split generic torsor the coefficient pushforward is induced; apply Shapiro and commute t* with derived invariants/orbits to identify restriction and trace.
Use the cup trace square and truncation bounds to lift the comparison needed for the duality morphism into the equivariant category, as in Lemmas 4.4.21–4.4.22.

Apply almost proper duality and the Hom/invariants–orbits adjunction; substitute the two torsor isomorphisms to obtain 𝒟_𝔛. Do not assume a G-equivariant action on the entire pushed-forward dualizing complex.

nodes.title: Top étale trace and almost detection
nodes.statement: A map between finite-dimensional F_p-vector spaces is an isomorphism exactly when its scalar extension to O_Cᵃ/p is an almost isomorphism. If X/C is connected smooth proper pure-d, the analytic torsion trace t_X:H²ᵈ_ét(X,F_p(d))→F_p imported from H3 is an isomorphism. proofSteps: A nonzero finite F_p-vector space becomes a nonzero almost O_C/p-module: multiplication by a sufficiently small nonzero ε∈𝔪_C does not kill O_C/p. Apply this to kernel and cokernel.
Use H⁰(X,F_p)=F_p and global almost duality to prove dim H²ᵈ(X,F_p)=1.

Use the nonzero/surjective geometric-fibre normalization of the existing analytic trace to identify the one-dimensional top trace as an isomorphism. The geometric-fibre nonvanishing beyond H3’s supplied trace is request R3.

nodes.title: Mod-p Poincaré duality
nodes.statement: Let K be complete rank one of mixed characteristic (0,p), C its completed algebraic closure, and X/K smooth proper pure of dimension d. For every i≥0 the cup product and analytic trace give a perfect Gal(C/K)-equivariant pairing Hⁱ_ét(X_C,F_p)⊗H^{2d−i}_ét(X_C,F_p(d))→F_p. All groups outside [0,2d] vanish. The trace on the top twisted group is an isomorphism when X is geometrically connected.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Reduce to C and a connected component; use the top trace isomorphism.
Compare the cup adjoint to its almost scalar extension via primitive comparison and finite-dimensional Hom base change.
Use degreewise almost duality and almost detection to prove bijectivity.
Recover the Galois action from the canonical étale trace and functorial cup products; do not choose a Galois-trivialization of the Tate twist.
acceptance: For P¹ the trace sends c₁(O(1)) to 1; in characteristic p the analogous p-torsion theorem is not asserted.

The residue-characteristic equality ℓ=p is allowed because char K=0. In characteristic p and positive dimension the Artin–Schreier sequence instead forces H²ᵈ(X_C,F_p)=0; Z Remark 1.1.5 is a scope test, not an extension of this theorem.

nodes.title: Poincaré duality for finite mod-p local systems
nodes.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, for every finite-rank étale F_p-local system L on X, cup, evaluation L⊗L∨→F_p and t_X give perfect Galois-equivariant pairings Hⁱ(X_C,L)⊗H^{2d−i}(X_C,L∨(d))→F_p. Duals, twists and evaluation use the existing local-system operations.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Trivialize monodromy on a finite Galois étale cover and pass to its Sylow-p intermediate cover, of degree prime to p.

The remaining p-group representation over F_p has a filtration with trivial one-dimensional quotients: its finite underlying set has a nonzero invariant by the existing p-group fixed-point congruence; repeat on the quotient.
Apply the constant theorem and the five lemma along that filtration, with evaluation and connecting-map signs.
Use restriction and finite étale trace to split L off the pushed-forward pullback: their composite is the prime-to-p degree, a unit.

Reuse the existing finite-dimensional p-group fixed-vector theorem in current Tau Ceti, Representation.exists_common_fixed_vector_of_isPGroup (RepresentationTheory.Unipotent.PowerOrder); the pinned Mathlib fixed-point theorem also supplies the finite F_p case. This algebraic input is not a new target owned here.

nodes.title: Perfect proper cohomology complexes
nodes.statement: For a proper rigid C-space of pure dimension d, not necessarily smooth, RΓ_ét(X,Z/pⁿ) is a perfect complex of Tor-amplitude [0,2d] for n≥1. RΓ_proét(X,Z_p)=Rlim_n RΓ_ét(X,Z/pⁿ) is perfect over Z_p with the same Tor-amplitude, and Hⁱ(X,Z_p)=lim_n Hⁱ(X,Z/pⁿ). Finite generation does not imply that these integral cohomology modules are torsion-free.
hypotheses: PD.0–PD.5 use the fixed mixed-characteristic rank-one valuation setting of the reader; every model, smoothness, reducedness, purity, boundedness and properness condition in this statement is part of the hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use the general proper singular primitive comparison/finiteness contract G3 to obtain finite mod-p cohomology in [0,2d]. The existing smooth P8 node alone does not give this scope.

Use the proper all-torsion projection formula to identify derived reduction of the constant-coefficient complex with mod-p cohomology. Apply pseudo-coherent/derived Nakayama perfectness and its Tor-amplitude criterion.
Pass through the derived p-complete inverse system to Z_p, retaining the same amplitude.
Finite finite-level cohomology gives the Mittag–Leffler condition, so the Milnor lim¹ term vanishes.
acceptance: A complex of projectives of amplitude [0,2d] can have torsion cohomology; the assertion does not give degreewise integral perfect pairings.

Use perfectness to commute duality with Λ_n→F_p base change; both cup and traces reduce compatibly.

nodes.title: Coherent integral reductions of disconnected bases
nodes.statement: For a totally disconnected perfectoid S=Spa(R,R⁺) over C and a pseudouniformizer ϖ∈R⁺, R⁺/ϖ is coherent. Thus an almost finitely generated submodule of an almost finitely presented R⁺/ϖ-module is almost finitely presented. For the strictly totally disconnected bases used below, O_S⁺/p is flat over R⁺/p on the étale site, and étale sheaves identify with sheaves on |S|.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Use the imported component description by affinoid fields and profinite component space.

Near any component a finitely generated ideal reduces to a principal ideal in a valuation-ring quotient with principal annihilator; extend the generators and relations over a clopen neighborhood and use compactness.

Approximate almost modules by finite presentations to obtain almost coherence. Flatness and the strictly disconnected site identification are imported from D1, not claimed for arbitrary perfectoid bases.
acceptance: Adic constructibility and Zariski constructibility differ: the complement of a classical point of a closed disc need not be quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Relative strict containment
nodes.statement: For affinoid U⊂V over an affinoid base S, U is strictly contained in V relative to S when every map Spa(K,O_K)→U over S whose projection extends to Spa(K,K⁺)→S, with K⁺ an open valuation subring, extends to a map Spa(K,K⁺)→V over S. The extended map is not required to land in U. In this layer U is a rational subset of V, and V maps to a relative ball through rational embeddings and finite étale maps.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Express the lifting condition over valuation field pairs using the existing adic morphisms.
Use the relative valuative description to compare with compact containment on the smooth affinoid charts used in nested proper covers.
acceptance: The larger target V in the extension is essential.

nodes.title: Finite presentation on relative smooth charts
nodes.statement: Let S=Spa(R,R⁺) be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid over C and let U=Spa(A,A⁺) map to the relative closed ball Bⁿ_S by a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, with the integral structures used in SW. Then A⁺/p is a finitely presented R⁺/p-algebra.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Approximate the chart and finite étale/rational maps by finite-presentation rigid spaces over C, using the perfectoid limit theorem.
Apply the Reduced Fibre input G2 after a rig-étale cover at finite level; it splits over the strictly disconnected S.
Geometrically reduced model fibres ensure that the power-bounded rings commute with these base changes; pass to the filtered colimit modulo p.
acceptance: Finitely presented as an algebra does not mean finitely presented as a module; the next containment theorem adds that stronger conclusion only for a factorization.

nodes.title: Finite presentation of restriction factorizations
nodes.statement: In the preceding chart setting let U=Spa(A,A⁺)⊂V=Spa(B,B⁺) be rational and strictly contained relative to S. Then B⁺/p→A⁺/p factors through a finitely presented R⁺/p-module. No claim that the image itself is finitely presented is made.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Work over a component valuation field and reduce to its residual valuation ring V=K⁺/K°°.
The image algebra of B in A is flat finitely generated over V, hence finitely presented; strict containment supplies its valuative properness and therefore finiteness.

Lift finitely many kernel generators, take powers killing their nilpotent images modulo p, and factor through a finite presented module algebra. Glue over clopens of the disconnected base. The valuation-ring finite-presentation and properness criterion are G5.
acceptance: The factorization has a module-finite middle object although source and target chart algebras are usually not module-finite.

nodes.title: Almost finite-presentation spectral-sequence factorization
nodes.statement: Let (E_i^{a,b}⇒M_i^{a+b})_{0≤i≤(N+1)3^{N+1}} be upper-right-quadrant spectral sequences over R⁺/p with compatible transition maps. If for some fixed page r every successive page-r map factors through an almost finitely presented module, then M_0^k→M_{(N+1)3^{N+1}}^k factors through such a module for k≤N. If the endpoint map is the identity of M, this proves M almost finitely presented.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: A three-step transition at page r gives a factorization on kernels and then cokernels through almost finitely presented modules; use almost coherence for both.
Iterate the three-step loss to reach the stable page in total degrees ≤N.
Pass through the N+1 filtration steps by pullback–pushout extensions to factor the abutment map.
An identity factorization makes M a retract of an almost finitely presented module; do not replace factorization by a claim about arbitrary images.
acceptance: For N=0 the specified chain length is 3; a single arbitrary page-r image statement is a different and stronger assertion.

nodes.title: Relative almost finite presentation of proper cohomology
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y be proper smooth between rigid spaces over C, L a finite F_p-local system, and S=Spa(R,R⁺)→Y a strictly totally disconnected quasi-pro-étale perfectoid. For every i≥0, Hⁱ(X_S,L⊗O⁺_{X_S}/p) is almost finitely presented over R⁺/p, for the pseudouniformizer almost convention of SW Proposition 10.5.2.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Choose enough nested affinoid covers with relative strict containment and good smooth coordinates; trivialize L on the finite étale charts.

Compute local almost cohomology by toric perfectoid covers and Koszul complexes. The local restriction maps factor through almost finite presentations by the preceding chart theorem and the explicit toric cohomology estimates.
Use the (i+1)3^{i+1} chain of spectral-sequence maps to factor the identity on Hⁱ through an almost finitely presented module. Retract closure proves the claim.
The local estimate is an extension of the absolute almost finite-generation proof; G5 records the explicit relative chain-level factorization verification still required.
acceptance: Almost finite generation alone would not supply the continuity criterion needed for a local system.

nodes.title: Local constancy from almost finite presentation
nodes.statement: In the preceding setting, suppose M=Hⁱ(X_S,L⊗O⁺/p) is almost finitely presented. Then (Rⁱf_ét,*L)|S is a finite F_p-local system. This criterion uses the all-p quasi-pro-étale base-change branch, the relative primitive comparison, and the topology of the strictly disconnected base; it makes no arbitrary proper-base-change assertion in advance.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Use quasi-pro-étale base change to identify the pulled-back étale direct image, and flatness of O_S⁺/p to associate the underived module sheaf M.

The elementary-divisor sequence of the fibre of M varies continuously in the sup norm, by almost finite presentation and valuation-ring elementary divisors. Primitive comparison makes each sequence consist of finitely many 1’s and then zeros; its rank is therefore locally constant.
Extend a stalk basis to sections. Kernels and cokernels of the resulting map are almost finitely presented by almost coherence; their discrete elementary-divisor sequences vanish on a neighborhood.
Detect the resulting F_p sheaf isomorphism by its field fibres, and descend along quasi-pro-étale covers. The elementary-divisor continuity proof is explicitly included in G5.
acceptance: Use C1’s quasi-pro-étale branch for p-torsion, not C3’s prime-to-p qcqs base-change theorem.

nodes.title: Proper smooth relative mod-p finiteness
nodes.statement: Let C be complete algebraically closed over Q_p and f:X→Y proper smooth between rigid C-spaces. For every finite-rank étale F_p-local system L and every i≥0, Rⁱf_ét,*L is a finite-rank étale F_p-local system. Its stalks are the cohomology of the geometric fibres. The ranks are locally constant; they may differ on connected components of Y.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Pull back to the basis of strictly totally disconnected quasi-pro-étale covers.
Apply relative almost finite presentation and the local-constancy criterion there.
Descend the finite local system along the site comparison; identify geometric stalks by the weak geometric proper-base-change theorem.
acceptance: No arbitrary p-adic local system is asserted to have finite free higher Z_p direct images.

nodes.title: Relative finite p-power and integral local systems
nodes.statement: For f as above and a finite free lisse Z_p-sheaf T, each Rⁱf_ét,*(T/pⁿ) is a locally constant finite Z/pⁿ-module sheaf. With the pro-étale inverse-limit interpretation, Rⁱf_proét,*T is a lisse finitely generated Z_p-module sheaf, with possible torsion. The required inverse-limit and stalk comparisons are part of this assertion; it does not declare every direct image finite free.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Induct on n using 0→T/p→T/pⁿ⁺¹→T/pⁿ→0 and the exact-sequence category of finite local systems.
Use finite stalk cohomology for the Mittag–Leffler argument and retain the derived inverse-limit sequence until lim¹ vanishes.

Import P8’s étale/pro-étale lattice equivalence and its lisse direct-image comparison. Extend from finite free lattices to finitely generated modules by their finite torsion submodule and free quotient, using H0’s finite local systems. D7 supplies the derived-limit/Mittag–Leffler algebra; no assertion about arbitrary inverse limits of sheaves is used.
acceptance: An extension in finite coefficient local systems need not be free over Z/pⁿ; torsion in integral fibre cohomology is permitted.

nodes.title: Zariski-constructible torsion complexes
nodes.statement: For a rigid K-space in characteristic zero and Λ=Z/n, n>0, an étale Λ-sheaf is Zariski-constructible when on every affinoid open it is finite locally constant on each stratum of some finite stratification by Zariski-locally closed rigid subspaces. D_zc^{(b)}(X,Λ) consists of complexes whose cohomology is Zariski-constructible and which are bounded on every qcqs open. On qcqs X this is D_zcᵇ. This is distinct from Huber’s adic constructibility on Boolean combinations of qc opens.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Use the existing rigid Zariski closed/locally closed subspace operations.
Define finite local constancy on strata using the existing étale local-system category.
Take the cohomological full derived subcategory and the locally bounded convention.
acceptance: Global boundedness cannot be imposed on every non-quasi-compact proper-map problem.

nodes.title: Locality and finite-cover generators
nodes.statement: Zariski-constructibility of finite torsion étale sheaves in characteristic-zero rigid geometry is étale local. On a qcqs X, D_zcᵇ(X,Z/n) is the thick triangulated subcategory generated by finite direct images f_*M of finite constant sheaves on finite Y→X. The affinoid algebraization input identifies these categories with constructible sheaves on Spec A when X=Spa A.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Use the affine constructible comparison G4 and the maximal lisse open; flat restriction maps preserve it, so the complement glues to a coherent closed subset.
Induct on dimension to prove locality, using descent of coherent ideals.

For generators, pass to a prime-to-ℓ finite étale cover on a dense lisse stratum, with unipotent residual monodromy, and extend it to a finite branched cover; use localization and direct summands. G4 includes the branched-cover extension theorem. The unipotent filtration is a finite-group representation argument; reuse current Tau Ceti’s fixed-vector results, or the pinned Mathlib fixed-point baseline, without invoking geometric Poincaré duality.
acceptance: Use the affinoid comparison owned by this Part II; its nonproper comparison and branched-cover input remain G4.

nodes.title: Zariski-constructible proper pushforward
nodes.statement: For any proper morphism f:X→Y of rigid spaces over a characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean field K, and any n>0, R f_* carries D_zc^{(b)}(X,Z/n) into D_zc^{(b)}(Y,Z/n). If source and target are qcqs, it carries bounded objects to bounded objects. The theorem allows residue characteristic dividing n.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Work over an affinoid target, use finite-cover generators, and reduce to the constant sheaf on a proper space.
Use rigid resolution and proper cohomological descent to replace a fixed cohomological degree by finitely many smooth hypercover terms.
Use proper generic smoothness G5 to find a dense Zariski open of the reduced target over which those proper maps are smooth.

For ℓ=p apply relative finiteness; for ℓ≠p use H3’s smooth proper prime-to-p local constancy. Induct over the closed complement and use weak geometric base change plus the uniform local cohomological bound. This proof does not use the arbitrary base change theorem it precedes.
acceptance: Over a non-qc target, neither global fibre dimension bounds nor one global cohomological interval are assumed.

nodes.title: Proper cohomology under algebraically closed field extension
nodes.statement: For C′/C/Q_p an extension of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, proper rigid X/C and F∈D_zcᵇ(X,Z/pᵃ), the canonical map RΓ(X,F)→RΓ(X_{C′},F_{C′}) is an isomorphism. The field extension need not have transcendence dimension zero.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Use finite generators and coefficient induction to reduce to F_p on a proper finite cover.
Use the singular proper primitive comparison G3 on both fields.
On a local toric perfectoid cover, compute O⁺/p cohomology by a finite Koszul complex; the scalar-extended integral perfectoid ring and the power-bounded base-change ring are almost isomorphic.
Glue the almost local comparison, then detect the finite F_p cohomology map by almost scalar extension. The local toric covering and singular comparison beyond the smooth case are part of G3.
acceptance: This field-extension step supplies the missing all-p comparison at rank-one geometric points in arbitrary proper base change.

nodes.title: Proper base change with all torsion coefficients
nodes.statement: In a cartesian square of rigid spaces over a complete characteristic-zero nonarchimedean field, with f:X→Y proper and arbitrary g:Y′→Y, let f′:X′→Y′ and g′:X′→X be the base changes. For every n>0 and F∈D_zc^{(b)}(X,Z/n), the canonical exchange map g^*R f_*F→R f′_*g′^*F is an isomorphism. No prime-to-residue-characteristic restriction is imposed.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Construct the exchange natural transformation from the site adjunctions, respecting composition.

Both sides are Zariski-constructible by proper pushforward and hence overconvergent; use enough rank-one geometric points and weak geometric proper base change to reduce the map to field-valued proper cohomology.
For residue-prime-to-n coefficients apply the inherited Huber theorem; for p-power coefficients use the algebraically closed field-extension comparison.
Use coefficient decomposition and local boundedness to conclude for all n and the stated derived range.
acceptance: The result is scoped to Zariski-constructible locally bounded complexes; it is not an arbitrary-sheaf p-torsion six-functor theorem.

nodes.title: Proper constant cohomology sheaves on smooth rigid bases
nodes.statement: Let K be complete algebraically closed over Q_p, g:Z→Spa K proper rigid, n≥1 and m≥0. On the big étale site of smooth rigid K-spaces, Rᵐg_ét,*(Z/n) is canonically the constant sheaf associated to Hᵐ_ét(Z,Z/n). Equivalently for a smooth Y/K the proper base-change sheaf on Y is the pullback of that finite module. This is a statement about sheaves, not equality of Hᵐ(Z×Y,Z/n) with Hᵐ(Z,Z/n) for all Y.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Apply all-torsion proper base change to Z×Y→Y for every smooth rigid Y.
Over algebraically closed K the small étale sheaf Rᵐg_*(Z/n) on Spa K is the constant module Hᵐ(Z,Z/n).
Pull back to Y and glue naturally in Y on the big étale site. Without algebraic closedness the correct base sheaf carries its Galois action.
acceptance: For Y with its own nonzero higher cohomology, the product cohomology need not be constant; only the higher direct-image sheaf is being identified.

nodes.title: Affinoid constructible algebraization
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic zero, A be a K-affinoid algebra, S_alg=Spec A and S=Spa(A,A°). For a finite-type S_alg-scheme Z and n≥1, analytification induces a fully faithful t-exact functor D_cᵇ(Z,Z/n)→D_zcᵇ(Z_an,Z/n); it is an equivalence when Z is proper over S_alg, in particular for Z=S_alg. For every finite-type map h:Z→W of finite-type S_alg-schemes, (Rh_*F)_an≅Rh_an,*F_an for F∈D_cᵇ(Z,Z/n), without a properness hypothesis on h. It also identifies the lisse subcategories for every such Z.
hypotheses: Use the field, base-space, coefficient, boundedness and morphism hypotheses in this statement; PD.6 uses C complete algebraically closed over Q_p, while PD.7 allows characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean K unless specialized to C.
proofSteps: Extend the existing H5 proper algebraic/analytic comparison to finite-type schemes over an affinoid algebra; the nonproper direct-image comparison and full faithfulness are G4, not consequences of proper comparison.
For proper Z, use induction over a normal lisse stratum. Extend its finite étale covers across the normalization as finite branched covers, algebraize by relative rigid GAGA, and restrict back.
Use finite descent and normal compactification to identify lisse subcategories on nonproper Z. G4 records the required branched-cover and comparison inputs.

AC 5.5.2/5.5.5–5.5.7 give the almost quotient adjunction and comparison on the target. G1 explicitly supplies universally coherent scheme duality.
Split Z’s specialization definition from AC 6.13.5–6.13.6, which supplies general almost coherence, reduction and dimension bounds; no smooth-only inference.
Added smoothness specifically to the C.9 nearby-cycle comparison and its API. C.4–C.8 support generic fibre and proper comparison without that extra hypothesis.
Restored separatedness from Z 2.4.1. Retains choice dependence of the complex, canonical bottom sheaf, derived reduction and amplitude.
Restored separatedness in the étale and algebraization assertions of Z 2.4.7–2.4.9; completeness itself has the broader scope of 2.4.6.
Z 2.5.1/2.5.2 define the kernel before an intersection notation is legitimate. The three tests distinguish compatible pairs from an unrestricted sum.
Made the canonical-sheaf separatedness explicit and replaced a vague hypothesis reference by the reduced-residue-fibre, dense-open reflexive statement of Z 2.5.4.
Restored separatedness of the models. Z 2.6.1–2.6.2 support compatible underived bottom traces, not a general formal f!.
Restricted the construction to algebraically closed K=C, as stipulated at the start of Z §2.7; retains reduced residue fibre and noncanonical complex comparison.
Restricted to C as in Z §2.7; replaced the nontrivial field-extension test by an identity test compatible with this base. Split-cover and torus tests retain degree normalization.
Z 3.2.1–3.2.2 quotient by scalar power torsion, not reduction modulo the scalar. Exterior cup products retain the p=2 argument.
Z 3.2.3–3.2.8 use derived completed cotangent transitivity on general models. The smooth isomorphism is a separate target.
Z 3.3.1–3.3.5 identify the image lattice and Fontaine twist; division onto that image precedes the Tate-valued inverse. Degree zero is specified separately.
Added the direct nice-model prerequisite and correction E21. Equations (3.6) and (3.7), the smooth square and torus test fix the inverse normalization without a residual scalar.

Z 3.5.1 requires separatedness, smooth pure generic fibre and reduced residue special fibre; the stronger qcqs convention is explicit. Made these conditions explicit in the smooth-model example. Modulo p need not be reduced.
Z 3.5.2–3.5.5 glue smooth and generic maps by Hartogs, then truncate and reduce derivedly; the target shift −2d is correct.
Z 3.6.1 includes almost amplitude in the definition. Generic finiteness alone is not substituted for it; the stated examples are 3.6.2.
Appendix D.3–D.13 gives exact finite pushforward and split-cover summation, integral limits, rationalization and finite-algebra trace. No degree inverse is used.
Z 3.6.4–3.6.6 support the integral and mod-p squares for rig-étale pseudo-finite maps; E6 repairs the formal-flatness cross-reference.
Separated qcqs pure-d polystable models are nice; polystability alone does not imply separatedness. Corrected that conclusion and canonical-line API.
Z 4.2.8/4.2.11 and (4.2)–(4.5) give the product-one group and perfectoid limit. Integral finite stages need not be flat over the chart.
Z 4.2.15/4.2.19 support additive decompositions after E13’s correction. The normalized nodal monomial product keeps its nonunit parameter.
Z 4.2.13/4.2.23–4.2.26 give characterwise Koszul cohomology and uniform annihilators; completed sums retain their uniform torsion requirements.
Z 4.2.27–4.2.30 turn the almost comparison into an honest décalage comparison. Scalar torsion brackets are distinguished from scalar quotients.
Z 4.3.1/4.3.3 define projection onto the base character summand. The normalization at 1 excludes the ordinary degree-divisible-by-p algebra trace.
Z 4.3.2/4.3.4–4.3.7 give derived Hom duality over the singular base; no false flatness or strong-grading premise is used. E15 fixes the stage index.
Z 4.3.9/4.3.13–4.3.14 support the top Koszul projection and character projection. Basis dependence is carried by the orientation line.
Z 4.3.10–4.3.15 use opposite-character derived duality and an almost sum-to-product comparison. The pairing is not declared honestly perfect before almostification.
Z 4.3.16–4.3.17 identify the geometric Faltings pairing and derived mod-p reduction. The canonical sheaf remains integral until reduction (E8).
Z 4.1.1 and §1.4 define perfection by both internal-Hom adjoints. The dualizing-complex target is not replaced by a projectivity assertion.
Z 4.4.3 uses nearby-cycle invariance, trace compatibility and almost proper duality. The input is a proper rig-isomorphism between nice models.
Z 4.4.2 retains finite quotient, quasiprojective residue fibre and generic G-torsor conditions. G2 owns quotient existence; PerfectoidQuotients Q0 does not.
Z 4.4.4/4.4.10/4.4.12/4.4.14 define derived invariants and orbits over the group algebra. The left/right conversion is explicit for nonabelian G.
Z 4.4.11/4.4.15 commute the indicated site pushforward with homotopy operations and identify contragredient Hom; no exactness of ordinary invariants is assumed.
Z 4.4.16–4.4.23 use induced torsor Shapiro objects for the orbit and invariant comparisons. They do not claim a norm isomorphism for arbitrary modules.
Z 4.4.1/4.4.24 use the altered-uniformization zigzag; niceness is retained from 4.1.2 (E10), and G2 explicitly leaves the geometric proof input open.
Z 5.2.1–5.2.3 construct the proper-model counit composite. The negative trace shift and model independence are retained.
Z 5.2.4–5.2.5 give derived and degreewise almost duality. Almost finite freeness follows from proper smooth primitive comparison, not from all almost coherent modules.
Z 5.3.3/5.4.2–5.4.3 detect finite F_p isomorphisms almostly; H3 supplies the analytic trace. The additional connected top-trace property is an explicit supplier contract.
Z 5.4.4 gives the stated geometric pairing, Tate twist and Galois action. Geometric connectedness is required for a single top-trace isomorphism.
Z 5.4.5 gives finite-local-system duality. Added explicit reuse of current Tau Ceti’s fixed-vector theorem instead of allocating the algebraic step anew.
Split the Z 5.5.1 citation from PS 3.17, which provides singular proper finiteness. Derived reduction and Mittag–Leffler preserve perfectness and allow integral torsion.
Z 5.5.2 after E14 gives the shifted derived pairing; scalar reduction is over Z/pⁿ, not a false derived reduction over Z_p.
Z 5.5.3/5.5.5 construct the compatible inverse-limit and rational traces. Top truncation supplies the derived trace to the correctly shifted coefficient module.
Z 5.5.4 after E14 gives perfect derived Z_p duality. Integral cohomology may have torsion; no degreewise free-module duality is asserted.
Z 5.5.6 after E14 follows by inverting p; field coefficients then give the degreewise perfect pairings.
SW 10.5.2 and 10.5.4–10.5.5 give coherence, almost submodule finiteness and the stated strict-base sheaf/flatness facts.
Corrected sourceId to SW. Lemma 10.5.8 defines extension into V, not necessarily U; higher-rank valuative tests distinguish it from ordinary inclusion.
SW 10.5.9 proves finite presentation as an algebra, not a module. Reassigned finite-stage approximation to PerfectoidSpaces P5/P6; power-bounded base change remains G2.
SW 10.5.8 gives module factorization of the restriction map under strict containment. G5 retains the valuation-base properness criterion input.
SW 10.5.6–10.5.7 give the finite spectral-sequence chain length and factorization conclusion. An identity retract suffices; image finiteness is not used.
SW 10.5.10 combines the finite charts, nested covers and spectral factorization for relative O⁺/p cohomology, retaining the strict perfectoid base.
SW 10.5.3 uses continuous elementary divisors and relative primitive comparison. G5 records the continuity proof; C1 is used only in its all-p quasi-pro-étale range.
SW 10.5.1 follows after strict-base descent and the preceding criterion; it does not assume the arbitrary proper p-torsion base change proved later.
Routed geometric lattice comparison to the exact P8 node, with finite torsion/free devissage; D7 supplies limit algebra. SW p. 82 supports finitely generated, possibly torsion, direct images.
Replaced unrelated BH 1.2/1.3 by Definition 3.1 and Warning 3.2. Locally bounded non-qc and bounded qcqs conventions remain distinct from Huber constructibility.
BH 3.5–3.7 use finite-cover unipotence, not geometric PD.5 duality. Replaced the unnecessary duality prerequisite by the fixed-vector/invariant baseline; G4 retains branched-cover extension.
BH 3.10 uses finite-range resolution descent, generic smoothness on the reduced target and PD.6. G5 retains BH 2.27/2.29 proof inputs.
BH 3.25 covers arbitrary algebraically closed field extensions using almost integral toric comparison, not only transcendence-dimension-zero base change. G3 retains the required local calculation.
BH 3.15 combines constructibility, geometric field extension and the separate prime-to-residue/p-primary branches. No circular use in PD.6 occurs.
Heuer Proposition 2.18 is on published p. 279 in volume 240, pp. 261–312. Corrected metadata and locator; the assertion concerns the big smooth étale sheaf, not global product cohomology.
BH 3.7 includes full faithfulness, proper essential surjectivity, lisse comparison and nonproper finite-type direct-image comparison. G4 explicitly retains the unread Hansen proof inputs.
